change.title: ao-replay/9076-r3
change.description: fix(devices): record the boot a helper was made for, read before it
change.author: Prasad-D-Ware

findings.title: Hub-start test no longer exercises EnsureReady's ordering
findings.body: TestHubStartRecordsEverySimulatorsBoot now calls currentBoots and storeBootsLocked directly, so it no longer goes through EnsureReady. The fix at provider.go:238-257 is the order: read the boots before startHub, store them after p.hub is set. Nothing tests that order. Moving the read after startHub, or dropping the store, would still pass. The test name also says 'hub start', which it no longer covers. Consider a test that drives EnsureReady with fake lookPath, ensureTool and startHub seams if they exist. If they don't, say in the test comment that it only covers the helpers.

findings.title: EnsureReady now waits on simctl synchronously while holding startMu
findings.body: The old code recorded boots in a goroutine with its own 30s timeout, bound to p.life. The new p.currentBoots(ctx) call at line 241 runs inline, under startMu and before the hub starts. It runs `xcrun simctl list` through p.run, bounded only by the caller's ctx. For EnsureReady's callers that is the request ctx (provider.go:559) or the 2-minute restart ctx (provider.go:1173). A slow or hung simctl delays hub start and every Boot or List waiting on startMu. If simctl fails, boots is nil and nothing is recorded, as before. Consider a short timeout for this read, for example 10s derived from ctx, so the read cannot hold up hub start.

contracts.action: EnsureReady reads simulator boots before starting the hub and stores them after p.hub is set, replacing the async recordBoots goroutine
contracts.equivalent_path: Old path: a goroutine called recordBoots after p.hub was set, reading simctl after the hub's helpers existed.
contracts.before_after: Before, the read came after hub start, so a reboot between hub start and the read was taken as the helpers' boot and missed. Now the read comes before startHub, so such a reboot reads as a change at the next NoteBooted. The store is under p.mu once p.hub is set and the hub is not closed. Boot and replaceHub go through EnsureReady and startMu, so Boot's store and EnsureReady's store are serialized.
contracts.visible_effect: No UI change. At worst one extra hub restart, and viewers reconnect.
contracts.failure_mode: If simctl fails, boots is nil and storeBootsLocked returns without storing, as the old code did. The cost is that EnsureReady now blocks on simctl, bounded by the caller's ctx.

contracts.action: Boot reads the simulator's boot after the hub boot call and before the grid start, then stores it once Boot ends
contracts.equivalent_path: Old path: recordBoots ran at the end of Boot, with its own 15s context, and read simctl after the helper existed.
contracts.before_after: Before, an outside reboot between the helper's start and the end of Boot was recorded as the helper's boot and missed. Now helperBoot is read before the helper is made, and stored after restoreQuality. A reboot during Boot is recorded by NoteBooted without a replacement because ownBoots is set. Boot's store then overwrites it with the helper's boot, so the next NoteBooted sees a change and replaces the hub. The ownBoots mark is cleared by the deferred function after the store, so there is no window without it.
contracts.visible_effect: A reboot outside AO during Boot's tail is now caught on the next device look.
contracts.failure_mode: If the simctl read fails or returns an empty lastUsedAt, helperBoot is empty and nothing is stored, as before. The store no longer has its own deadline, because it no longer calls simctl.

summary: The change moves boot recording to a read before the helper is made and a store afterwards. I found no defect in the logic. In EnsureReady the read happens before startHub, and the store runs under p.mu once p.hub is set. In Boot the read comes before the grid start, and the store happens before the deferred ownBoots clear. Two things are worth a look. The EnsureReady test now covers only the two helpers, not their order in EnsureReady. EnsureReady now waits on simctl inline while holding startMu, where it used to record boots in a goroutine.
